concierge.title: We'll switch you on — and off — ourselves.
concierge.description: Send us what you've got — one clean export or a decade of messy tabs — and one of us maps the columns and brings your divers in with you, free, on any plan. And if DiveDay is ever not the right fit, the door swings the other way just as personally: your data is yours, and we'll help you carry all of it back out. Getting in, and getting out, shouldn't be the hard part.

hub.title: The door swings both ways.
hub.description: Most shops stay on a spreadsheet, or software they've outgrown, because moving looks painful. These guides make the move concrete: how to get your divers out of whatever you use now, exactly what comes across into DiveDay, and what — honestly — stays behind.
hub.spreadsheetDescription: Running the day on a spreadsheet and a clipboard? Bring the sheet you already keep — and add the jobs a list can't do, like checking every card before the boat leaves.
hub.dontSeeSystemBody: Most exports import as-is — a spreadsheet of your divers with recognizable name, card, and size columns is all it takes. Try the live demo, or start a trial and bring a CSV: DiveDay maps the common column names, previews the file, and flags anything it doesn't recognize before saving.

competitor.scopeTableTitle: What comes across — and what doesn't
competitor.scopeTableDescription: This is the same scope table DiveDay shows before it imports a single row. A card your system already checked comes across verified and flagged imported, ready to use, with a one-tap confirm for staff, and its refresher-due date comes with it. A specialty card is the one that waits on that confirm before it clears the dive it authorizes; individual medical answers are never reconstructed.
competitor.bringFileIntro: With your export saved, the rest is in DiveDay and takes minutes.
competitor.openSettingsBody: In your DiveDay shop, the owner or manager opens the import page and uploads the CSV you exported.
competitor.checkPreviewBody: DiveDay maps your columns automatically and previews the file before anything is saved — how each column landed, which cards will come in verified and flagged imported, and anything it's leaving behind. Rows with an email match an existing diver so a re-import updates them instead of duplicating; the rows that pass import when you confirm.
competitor.importReadyBody: Roster, rental sizes, and cards are ready immediately: cards land verified and flagged imported, so divers are trip-ready from the first booking. Each imported card carries a one-tap confirm on the diver's record for staff to give it a look when they get a moment — no boarding waits on it. The one thing that does wait is a dive that requires a specialty card: that gate opens when a staffer confirms the card, which is one tap on the diver's record.

spreadsheet.title: The spreadsheet got you this far.
spreadsheet.heroLede: It won't flag the diver on tomorrow's boat whose card nobody's verified, chase the waiver no one signed, or let a diver book their own seat on a Sunday night. DiveDay reads the sheet you already keep — your divers, their cards, their sizes — and takes the rest off your hands. No system to rip out first; you already have the file.
spreadsheet.wedgeIntro1: A spreadsheet is a good memory and a bad teammate. It holds names and numbers, but it can't do the work that actually keeps a dive day calm and safe — the part you're doing by hand right now, in your head and across a stack of paper.
spreadsheet.wedgeIntro2: That's the trade DiveDay makes worth it. Not a prettier list — the jobs a list can't hold:

cardsChecked.title: Every card checked before the boat leaves
cardsChecked.body: DiveDay re-reads each diver's certification against what the trip and the site require, and the ones who can't board yet surface on their own — no scanning a column and hoping.

blockersOnePlace.title: The day's blockers in one place
blockersOnePlace.body: One screen shows who still can't board and why — a missing waiver, a card to verify — so nothing is remembered at the dock instead of the desk.

diversBookThemselves.title: Divers book and sign themselves
diversBookThemselves.body: A diver picks a seat and signs the waiver from a link, no account and no app — the signature chase at the dock mostly disappears.

manifestHeadCount.title: A manifest that's a head count, not a printout
manifestHeadCount.body: The captain checks divers off dive by dive on a phone — working from a copy saved to it before the boat leaves, so roll call keeps going when the signal doesn't, then checks itself against the live manifest when service returns.

spreadsheet.columnsTitle: Does your sheet have these columns?
spreadsheet.columnsIntro: One row per diver, and columns for what you know about them. Your headings don't have to match anything — DiveDay recognizes the common names, previews the file, and flags anything it doesn't before saving. If you'd rather start from a clean sheet, download one that's already in the right shape.

name.detail: First and last in two columns, or one full-name column — either works. This is the only thing a row truly needs.

email.detail: How DiveDay reaches a diver and recognizes a returning one, so a second import updates them instead of making a duplicate. A row without one still comes in as a new diver.

phone.detail: Mobile or landline, however you've written it.

emergencyContact.detail: A name and a phone number, when you have them, land on the diver's card.

diveInsurance.detail: However you keep it — a DAN number, a provider name — comes across as written. It's never a gate; it's what the crew wants on hand in an incident.

certification.detail: Agency, level, and card number. The card number is what lets a card come across at all — it arrives verified and flagged imported, ready to use, with a one-tap confirm for staff.

refresherDue.detail: If you track a refresher date on a card, it comes across with it — written however your sheet writes dates (05/04/2030, 4-May-2030, 2030-05-04). A date already past lands as a card that's due, which is the point. A date we can't read lands the card for staff review rather than as verified: we won't guess at a date the boat depends on.

specialty.detail: Deep, wreck, night, or drysuit — one cell can name several (“Deep, Wreck”) and each becomes its own card under the diver's agency number. They arrive verified and flagged imported, and the dive that needs one opens once a staffer confirms they've seen that card.

nitrox.detail: A yes/no column, plus the nitrox card number if you keep one — the card number is what actually brings it across, imported as a verified nitrox card. The Nitrox fill gives plain air until a staffer confirms they've seen that card.

rentalSizes.detail: BCD, wetsuit, boot, and fin — whatever sizes you already track become a fit profile.

pastVisits.detail: Keep a booking log? A date column, plus what you called the trip and what you charged, turns each row into that diver's history here — so a regular arrives as a regular. Repeat the diver's email on each of their rows; that's how the rows find the right person. It's history, not schedule: imported visits never become trips, and a booking you'd written off as cancelled still reads cancelled.

spreadsheet.scopeTableTitle: What comes across — and what doesn't
spreadsheet.scopeTableDescription: This is the same scope table DiveDay shows before it imports a single row. A card already in your sheet was checked by you, so DiveDay trusts it: cards come across verified and flagged imported, with a one-tap confirm for staff — and their refresher-due dates come with them. A specialty card is the one that waits on that confirm before it clears the dive it authorizes. Individual medical answers are never reconstructed.

The rows that pass import when you confirm.
spreadsheet.importReadyBody: Roster, rental sizes, and cards are ready immediately: cards land verified and flagged imported, so divers are trip-ready from the first booking. Each imported card carries a one-tap confirm on the diver's record for staff to give it a look when they get a moment — no boarding waits on it. The one thing that does wait is a dive that requires a specialty card: that gate opens when a staffer confirms the card, which is one tap on the diver's record.

about.heroDescription: DiveDay isn't a side product inside a bigger company, or a roadmap set by a committee that's never seen a boat. It's built by a small team of divers, with one founder accountable for every call it makes.
about.founderP1: A dive shop owner walked me through an ordinary day: a whiteboard for tomorrow's boat, a clipboard for the manifest, a spreadsheet someone updates by hand, and a couple of apps that don't talk to each other. He was paying for all of it twice — once for the software, again in the hours it pulled away from his divers. None of that was on him or his crew; they run a tight operation. The tools just never showed up for this industry.
about.founderP2: That's the pattern once you look for it: an entire industry running on software nobody actually built for it. What exists is dated at best and hostile at worst — built for a back office, not a wet dock. So shops keep the whiteboard and the clipboard, because paper never crashes, never logs you out, and never makes you tap through five screens with wet hands.
about.founderP3: DiveDay exists to close that gap: software fast enough, clear enough, and forgiving enough that a crew reaches for it without being told to — built by watching how a boat day actually runs, not around a spec written far from the water. If your team wouldn't open it on a busy morning, it hasn't done its job.
about.runP1: Write in about a bad morning at the counter and you reach the founder — not a queue, not a ticket number, not a form that asks you to attach a screenshot before anyone reads it. The person who answers is the person who can fix it.
about.runP2: The pricing works the same way: one flat number, no seats to count, no tier that hides the feature you actually need. Nobody here is compensated for selling you more, so the pricing page has nothing to hide behind.
about.rulesTitle: Four rules, and you can check every one.
about.rulesDescription: A new vendor can't point at customers, so these aren't promises — they're things you can go and test in the demo in about five minutes.

survivesDock.title: It has to survive the dock.
survivesDock.body: Wet hands, bright sun, one bar of signal, a boat that's already late. If a screen only works sitting down in an office, it hasn't been finished.
survivesDock.check: save a manifest to your phone, turn the network off, and run roll call anyway.

noSilentPasses.title: No silent passes.
noSilentPasses.body: Software that quietly waves a diver through because a field was blank is worse than paper. When DiveDay can't verify something, it says so and stops — and says which thing.
noSilentPasses.check: open the blockers queue and read why each name is on it.

onePrice.title: One price, no seats.
onePrice.body: Everything the product does is in the price. There is no tier that hides the feature you actually need, and nobody here is paid to sell you more of it.
onePrice.check: read the pricing page. It's one number and one list.

yourRecords.title: Your records are yours.
yourRecords.body: The export isn't a retention lever we release when you threaten to leave. It's a button, it works on day one of a trial, and it hands back documented files rather than a proprietary dump.
yourRecords.check: start a trial and download the ZIP before you've entered anything.

about.plainlyTitle: What we're not going to pretend.
about.plainlyDescription: You are going to find these out anyway. Better here, before you've moved a season of bookings.

new.title: DiveDay is new.
new.body: There is no install base to point at and no wall of logos to borrow credibility from. That is exactly why the demo is a real working shop and the export button works on your first day.

notEverything.title: It doesn't do everything.
notEverything.body: No retail register, no agency sync, no gear inventory. Those are real jobs done by other software, and pretending otherwise would only waste a season of yours.

stillMoving.title: It's still moving.
stillMoving.body: Early access means the shops that join first steer what gets built next, not a roadmap set months in advance in a room far from the water. That's the trade: a product that bends toward your season, and one that is still changing while you use it.

about.leaveP1: Trusting a small vendor with the records that get your divers on a boat is a real decision, so here are the parts of it worth knowing before you make it — including the one that matters most, which is how you'd walk away.
about.leaveP2: {terms} Coming the other way, a person will sit with your old export or spreadsheet and bring your divers across with you.
about.whoBuildsValue: Aaron Buxbaum, founder — a software engineer (Google Maps, a biotech company through its IPO, self-driving cars) and an obsessive diver. The person accountable for every call DiveDay makes.
about.whereLiveValue: On servers in the United States, and in a download you can take at any time.
about.committingValue: Month to month, per location, cancel whenever. No setup fee, no contract to get out of.
about.whoAnswersValue: The founder, directly. Founding shops get that in writing on the pricing page.
about.closingTitle: The honest way to judge all of this is to go use it.
about.closingDescription: No call, no form first. Walk a full sample shop as the owner, the captain, or a diver, and decide whether it feels like something your crew would open on a busy morning.

product.heroTitle: From the first booking to the last head count.
product.heroDescription: DiveDay is organized around the trip itself. Every booking, waiver, certification, payment, packing decision, and roll-call event stays attached to the people going out on the boat.
product.readinessTitle: One readiness answer, shared everywhere it matters.
product.readinessDescription: The front desk sees why a diver is blocked. The captain sees the same answer on the manifest. No one has to guess whether a missing waiver or pending card is okay to ignore.
product.readinessStep1: The trip and the dive site decide what each diver needs.
product.readinessStep2: If something can't be verified, DiveDay says so plainly — no silent passes.
product.readinessStep3: Staff fix the problem at the desk, not at the dock.
product.readinessMockupLabel: The DiveDay readiness section used by a dive shop's front desk.
product.systemTitle: Built around how a dive shop actually works.
product.dockTitle: A manifest that stays useful after the signal disappears.
product.dockDescription: The crew gets big phone controls, head counts for every dive, blockers that can't be ignored, a boarding history that keeps every correction, and a print view straight from the same manifest.
product.dockNote: The crew saves the manifest to their phone before leaving the dock. Anything marked offline stays clearly labeled until DiveDay is back in service and double-checks it against the live manifest — nothing is ever quietly overwritten.
product.captainPhoneLabel: A captain using the mobile roll-call view in DiveDay.
product.paymentTitle: The money runs through your Stripe account, not ours.
product.paymentDescription: Divers pay when they book, or leave a deposit and settle the balance at the dock. Staff raise an invoice at the counter for a trip, a course, rentals, nitrox, or a retail line. When a diver cancels inside the window you published, the refund goes back automatically — and when they don't, the page says so before they commit rather than after.
product.yourAccountBody: Payouts, disputes, and history stay in the Stripe account you already control. DiveDay never sits between you and the payment — and there is no per-booking cut on top of the flat price.
product.pricedBody: Payment is part of the same readiness answer as the waiver and the card, so “are they ready?” means all of it. Nobody boards on an assumption that someone else already settled up.
product.recapTitle: The day ends with a recap divers want to share.
product.recapDescription: The paperwork is DiveDay's job; the memory is the diver's. The night before, every diver gets a plain-language brief — dock time, conditions on the water, what to bring, who to text. After the trip, each diver gets their own recap page to keep and share.
product.nightBeforeTitle: A brief in plain words, not a form letter
product.nightBeforeBody: When to be at the dock, what the water looks like, what to pack, and who to text if something changes — written gently enough for someone's first boat dive.
product.afterTripTitle: A recap page they'll want to share
product.afterTripBody: The sites they dived, a shout-out from the crew, and room for their own photos — with a nudge to bring a buddy next time. Divers share it; the shop gets remembered.
product.boxDescription: No tiers, no add-ons, nothing here held back for a bigger plan. Every line is something you can go and do in the demo right now — open it in another tab and check us on any of them.
product.noDescription: You're sizing up a vendor you've never heard of; the least we can do is draw our own boundaries before you find them.

pos.title: A retail point of sale
pos.detail: Keep the register you have. You can put a retail line on a DiveDay order, but there's no barcode scanner or stock count here — DiveDay runs the water side of the shop.

gearSerials.title: Gear serial numbers
gearSerials.detail: DiveDay tracks every diver's sizes and builds the trip's packing list. It doesn't manage individual rigs or service history.

agencyLine.title: A live line to PADI or SSI
agencyLine.detail: No agency offers software a way to verify a C-card automatically, so verification stays honest: staff look the card up with the agency and mark it certified themselves.

product.closingTitle: Try it as the person doing the work.
product.closingDescription: Walk the live demo as the owner, the captain, or a diver — then start a trial shop of your own.
product.spreadsheetLink: On a spreadsheet today? Bring it across — we'll even do it with you →

pricing.heroTitle: One flat price for the whole shop.
pricing.heroDescription: No setup fee, no per-seat math, no feature tiers — the safety workflow is never an add-on you have to remember to buy.
pricing.feesNote: Payment-processing fees stay between you and your payment provider. If a future integration ever costs extra, we'll say so clearly before you turn it on.
pricing.includedTitle: Everything needed to run the current DiveDay workflow.
pricing.faqTitle: The questions that actually decide it.

whatIncluded.question: What is included?
whatIncluded.answer: The founding-shop price covers every currently available DiveDay workflow, from public bookings through the offline-ready boat manifest. It is not a collection of separate per-feature add-ons.

billing.question: How does billing work?
billing.answer: Month to month, per location. Cancel whenever you like and leave with your shop's records through the export button — no setup fee and no annual contract.

seeBefore.question: Can I see it before I commit?
seeBefore.answer: Yes. Open the live demo to see the day as the shop owner, an instructor, a divemaster, the captain, or a diver — it's a shop already full of sample trips. Or start a trial shop of your own: it begins empty, ready for your first trip.

offline.question: Does the manifest work offline?
offline.answer: Yes. The crew saves the manifest to their phone before leaving the dock. Departure and after-dive roll calls work from that copy, the screen always shows how fresh it is, and when service returns DiveDay checks every change against the live manifest before it counts.

dataIfNotWorking.question: DiveDay is new. What happens to my data if this doesn't work out?
dataIfNotWorking.answer: You leave with your shop's records, whenever you choose. {claim} {terms}

switching.question: What does switching to DiveDay actually involve?
switching.answer: Export a spreadsheet of customers from your current system, and DiveDay's importer brings in your divers, their certification cards, their rental sizes, and any waivers your old system already had signed — showing you exactly what will happen before anything is saved. When it recognizes an email it updates the existing diver instead of duplicating them. Imported cards arrive as claims for your staff to verify; a waiver your old system already had signed comes over marked as imported, so nobody has to sign it again. Step-by-step guides cover EVE, DiveShop360, DiveAdmin, and Smartwaiver.

agency.question: Does DiveDay connect to PADI or SSI?
agency.answer: No — no agency offers shop software a way to verify a C-card automatically, so DiveDay doesn't pretend. A photo of the card goes on the diver's profile once, your staff confirm the number with the agency and mark it certified, and that card stays with the diver for every future booking. Courses arrive as your shop's copy of the agency catalog, with DiveDay's published page templates as a starting point — you set the prices and choose what's visible.

pos.question: Does DiveDay replace my POS?
pos.answer: No — keep your register. DiveDay runs the water side of the shop: bookings, courses, readiness, trip prep, and the boat, with trip and course payments through your shop's own Stripe account. You can put a retail line on a DiveDay order, but there is no register, barcode scanner, or stock count here, and we'd rather say that plainly than pretend.

whyFounding.question: Why be a founding shop?
whyFounding.answer: Because early shops steer — what your crew runs into shapes what ships next. Founding shops also lock in today's price for two years and get a founder-direct line with same-day responses; every new feature lands in the one plan there is, with no higher tiers to move things into.

multipleLocations.question: What about multiple locations?
multipleLocations.answer: Each DiveDay workspace runs one shop today. If you operate more than one location, email aaron@dive.day — we'd rather build that with you than pretend it's already here.

pricing.stillQuestion: Still have a question a FAQ can't answer? Founding shops get a founder-direct line — use it, always welcome.
